New: free CLI, Python library and MCP wrapper, no server needed →

A reliability layer between AI agents and the APIs they call.

Every call claims a slot in Redis (SET NX) before it is forwarded, so a retry or a parallel duplicate gets the first result back instead of a second charge. Policies, spend caps and human approval decide whether a call runs at all. Every decision is written to Postgres and exported to Prometheus and OpenTelemetry. Self-hosted and open source; about 2 ms added per call.

Open source · no server

Start in 60 seconds. No account, nothing to deploy.

Three free tools in one package. Find the calls your agent would run twice, fix them with a decorator backed by your own SQLite or Redis, and wrap any MCP server so its write tools run once. Add the server later, when your team wants the dashboard, audit trail and approvals.

1 · FIND agentraas-chaos
terminal
# drops the response to each write after it executes,
# then reports what your code ran twice
$ pip install agentraas
$ agentraas-chaos --mock -- python my_agent.py

  DUPLICATES: 1 action(s) executed more than once
    2x  POST /v1/charges
  Protected by an idempotency key: 2 retries

Exits non-zero on a duplicate, so it fails CI. GitHub Action: sumedhchatse/agentraas/src/chaos-action@main

2 · FIX @exactly_once
agent.py
from agentraas.local import exactly_once

@exactly_once()  # SQLite by default, or RedisStore
def charge(customer, amount, idempotency_key=None):
    return stripe.Charge.create(
        customer=customer, amount=amount,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,  # same on every retry
    ).id

charge("cus_1", 4200)  # runs
charge("cus_1", 4200)  # cached, no second charge

Retries, concurrent duplicates and lost responses covered. Python today; TypeScript coming.

3 · WRAP agentraas wrap

Put it in front of any MCP server in Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client. An identical call to a write tool inside a 10-minute window returns the first result instead of running again, so a looping agent can't open the same issue or send the same email twice. Read-only tools always run. Every tool call lands in a local audit log.

Listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.sumedhchatse/agentraas.

The problem

Your agent didn't fail. The network did, and nobody told it.

Payment retry

Your n8n workflow hits Stripe. It times out. n8n retries.

The customer is charged twice, and you find out from a support ticket, not a log.

CRM duplicate

Your agent creates a HubSpot contact. The response is lost. It retries.

Two duplicate contacts, a messier pipeline, and a sales team that stops trusting the data.

Client update

Your agent sends a client a status update. The confirmation times out. It retries.

The client gets the same update twice, and starts wondering what else is off.

Team notification

Your agent posts an approval request to Slack. The webhook times out. It retries.

Your team approves the same request twice, or gets paged twice for one incident.

How it works

A dedup slot claimed atomically, before anything real happens.

Copy while the first is in flight: 409 Conflict, never forwarded.Forward times out: slot kept as "outcome unknown", never retried blindly.Process crashes mid-call: the slot's lease expires and the next copy reports outcome unknown.
01

Your agent sends the request to AgentRaaS instead of the API directly.

02

AgentRaaS atomically claims a dedup slot for that exact request in Redis.

03

First call: forwarded to the real API, and the result is cached.

04

Retry or duplicate: the cached result comes back. Never a second real execution.

Why not DIY idempotency keys?

Calling Stripe by hand? Its Idempotency-Key header is enough.

The case for AgentRaaS is narrower: not every provider has native idempotency (Twilio, Slack, most CRMs and your own endpoints don't), no-code tools can't set the header at all, and none of them give you one audit trail across services.

MCP-native

MCP is how agents call tools now. AgentRaaS speaks it natively.

A stalled MCP tool call gets retried just like a stalled HTTP request: same double-execution risk, different protocol. The MCP gateway applies the same atomic dedup guarantee to every tool call from Claude Desktop, Cursor, LangChain, AutoGen or CrewAI.

When AgentRaaS is down

Fail-closed by design, not fail-silent.

AgentRaaS sits in the request path. If it's unreachable, your call fails; it never silently succeeds un-deduped. There is no fallback anywhere in the SDK, the n8n node or the MCP gateway that quietly calls Stripe or Twilio directly. Routing around an outage would mean the exact retry-storm double charge this product exists to prevent, at the moment you'd least want it. Treat it like any other dependency on your critical path.

FAQ

Questions people actually ask

The short answers. Full detail is in the docs and LICENSE.md.

Do I need to pay anything?

No. Self-hosting is free and open source with every feature and no action limit, and the free tools (library mode, chaos tester, MCP wrap) need no account at all. On AgentRaaS Cloud the first 500 actions each month are free; past that it's $1 per 1,000 actions that run, up to a monthly cap you set.

Is self-hosted really unlimited?

Yes. On your own infrastructure there is no cap, no metering and no phone-home check, and every feature is included with no license token. Only AgentRaaS Cloud is metered, because it runs on our servers.

How does pay as you go work on Cloud?

You're billed once a month for the actions that actually ran: forwarded and completed. Duplicates AgentRaaS caught, calls blocked by a policy or limit, and calls waiting for approval are free. The first 500 each month are free, then $1 per 1,000, charged in whole thousands with the rest carried to next month. You set a monthly cap, and calls stop at it instead of running up a bill. Paid usage opens soon; until then Cloud accounts are free up to 500 actions a month. There are no plans or tiers: every Cloud account gets every feature. For a contract or SLA-backed support, email hello@agentraas.io.

Is my data safe if I self-host?

Self-hosted means your audit log, credentials, and traffic never leave infrastructure you control. We don't see any of it. Stored credentials are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM), PII/DLP redaction can run before anything touches the audit log, and the log is tamper-evident and SIEM-exportable for compliance-sensitive teams.

Do you support n8n, Make, or Zapier?

Yes. No-code tools work the same way code does: point the HTTP Request node at your AgentRaaS URL instead of the API directly. No custom node install required for any of them.

What happens if my agent retries a request?

AgentRaaS claims an atomic dedup slot in Redis before anything real happens. The first call gets forwarded and its result cached; any retry or duplicate, even a concurrent one, gets the cached result back instead of a second real execution. This is tested under real concurrent load, not just claimed (see src/api-gateway-rs/test/dedup.test.js).

Is this open source?

Yes. The server is AGPL-3.0 and the SDKs are MIT/Apache-2.0. The advanced features (SSO, approvals, DLP, HMAC) are under the Functional Source License: free to self-host for any purpose except a competing hosted service, and Apache-2.0 after two years. Self-hosting includes every feature, with no license token. See LICENSE.md for the exact terms.

What does "agentgateway-compatible" mean?

agentgateway (a Linux Foundation project) is an edge proxy for AI traffic: auth, RBAC, rate limiting, and observability across all your MCP/tool servers, not just AgentRaaS. If you already run it (or want to), AgentRaaS drops in as a backend behind it with zero code changes on either side. See Getting started for the one-command setup. Most self-hosters don't need this; it matters once you're managing more than one MCP server behind a shared gateway.
